doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Group playing, Town Hall and the White House
title: Jim Hall and Friends at Town Hall

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: How are we doing on time? Kimery: We have about 15 minutes.

Okay. Let’s talk about… Oh, let’s talk a little bit about that Live at Town Hall. Mostly because it was one of those eclectic concerts where you… it was Jim Hall and friends, and you had so many different people in combinations on one concert.
Oh.
And I can tell you who they all are, if you need any memory.
Yeah, just to refresh.
Well, you did some duos with Ron, and you did some duos with Brookmeyer.
Oh, yeah.
Gerry Mulligan was there.
Oh, yeah.
Don Thompson played a little piano, as well.
Really talented guys there. (laughs)
There was nobody with any talent. Gary Burton.
Yeah.
Steve was there. LaSpina. Terry Clarke. And the Classic Heritage Ensemble. I think you did Thesis that night.
Oh, yeah, yeah.
Was it Kermit Moore?
Kermit Moore, yeah, who I had gone to school with in Cleveland. That was great.
Gil Goldstein. And then just to round things out at the other extreme, you had Mick Goodrick, John Abercrombie…
Oh, yeah.
Peter Bernstein and John Scofield.
Oh, yeah. I forgot about that, yeah.
So it’s all a June concert in New York City at Town Hall.

That’s right. Yeah, I had forgotten… I remember one time looking behind and there were… with all these guitar players. There was a stack of amplifiers. And I said to the audience, I said, “This is not as dangerous as it looks. We have a non-proliferation treaty here. (laughs) It’s not gonna get too…” Yeah, that, that was great.
Talk about these guys. There were some interesting guitarists there.
Yeah. Some inter… yeah. Well, John Abercrombie—he’s got an incredible sense of humor, and I really admire him a lot and… Was Scofield there, as well? I forgot.
Mm-hmm.

Yeah. Great players. And Pete Bernstein was… (laughs) You know, he was three years old or something. I just… I had met Pete at the New School. He was in one of my ensembles there, and I just kinda wanted to, to show him off. So he, he was there. Then my…
What did you hear as a guitarist of your style and history… what do you hear in Mick Goodrick and Scofield? What is it that turns you on?
Well, each one is different from the other and… I thought that was kind of important, too. I’m trying to think about it.
Okay.
